review.explanation: The mention 向秀 is a direct full-name reference to the Wei-Jin philosopher Xiang Xiu. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-04-wenxue-036-liu-annotation-002) explicitly compares 支遁 to 向秀, noting both admired Zhuangzi and Laozi. The annotation text '遁比向秀雅尚莊老二子異時風尚玄同也' directly names 向秀 as the historical referent. The evidence specifically supports this identity resolution.

The surface 王 is the surname abbreviation of 王逸少 (Wang Xizhi). In the main text (sfh1-ev-04-wenxue-036-main), the full name 王逸少 appears at the start, and subsequent occurrences of 王 refer to the same person. The text '孫興公謂王曰' and '王本自有一徃雋氣' clearly show 王 referring to 王逸少. The evidence specifically supports this identity.

The surface 君 is the second-person pronoun used by 支道林 when addressing 王逸少. In the main text (sfh1-ev-04-wenxue-036-main), the passage '支語王曰君未可去貧道與君小語' shows 支道林 addressing 王 (who is 王逸少) as 君. The pronoun reference is clearly anchored to 王逸少 through the preceding context. The evidence specifically supports this identity.

The surface 王逸少 is the courtesy name of Wang Xizhi (王羲之). The main text (sfh1-ev-04-wenxue-036-main) opens with '王逸少作㑹稽' and the entire narrative revolves around this person. The courtesy name 逸少 is a well-established alias for 王羲之. The evidence specifically supports this identity resolution.

records.explanation: 莊周 (Zhuangzi) is a direct full-name reference to the philosopher Zhuang Zhou. He is distinct from the surname 莊 in annotation 002 which refers to 莊周 as one of the '二子' (two masters) alongside 老 (Laozi). The annotation mentions 莊周 in the context of 支法師's study of Zhuangzi's 逍遥 concept.

七沙門 refers to the seven Buddhist monks (including 支遁) who are compared to the 竹林七賢 (Seven Worthies of the Bamboo Grove) in the 道賢論. This is a collective descriptive reference, distinct from the group of Seven Worthies.
支 is the surname abbreviation of 支道林, used in the phrase 支道林㧞新領異... and later 孫與支共載. It corefers with the full name 支道林.
向秀 (Xiang Xiu) is a direct full-name reference to the Wei-Jin philosopher. The annotation compares 支遁 (Zhi Dun) to 向秀, noting both admired Zhuangzi and Laozi. He is distinct from 莊 and 老.
孫興公 is the full name of Sun Xinggong, who speaks to Wang about Zhi Daolin. He is distinct from both Wang and Zhi.
支法師 is an office/title reference to 支道林 (Zhi Daolin), the Buddhist monk. The annotation discusses his study of Zhuangzi's 逍遥 concept. This refers to the same person as 支道林 in the main text.
王 is the surname abbreviation of 王逸少 (Wang Xizhi), appearing at the start of the main text. It refers to the same person as the full name 王逸少.

君 is the second-person pronoun used by 支道林 when addressing 王逸少. 支語王曰君未可去 (Zhi said to Wang: 'You may not leave yet').
竹林七賢 refers to the Seven Worthies of the Bamboo Grove, a famous group of Wei-Jin literati. This is a collective descriptive reference, distinct from the group of seven Buddhist monks (七沙門).
王逸少 is the full name of Wang Xizhi (Wang Yishao), the protagonist of the main text. He is coreferent with the surname 王 in the main text. He is distinct from 支道林 and 孫興公.
莊 is a surname abbreviation referring to 莊周 (Zhuangzi), coreferent with the full name 莊周 in annotation 001. It appears in the phrase 莊老二子 (the two masters Zhuang and Lao), paired with 老.
老 is a surname abbreviation referring to 老子 (Laozi). It appears in the phrase 莊老二子 (the two masters Zhuang and Lao), paired with 莊. Laozi is distinct from Zhuangzi and from 向秀.
貧道 is a humble self-reference used by Buddhist monks. Here 支道林 uses it to refer to himself when speaking to 王逸少: 貧道與君小語 (let me have a brief talk with you). It corefers with 支道林.
支道林 is the full name of the Buddhist monk Zhi Daolin, introduced at the beginning of the story as being present at 㑹稽.
